newsitem.title: USA: NBA-RODMAN SUSPENDED AT LEAST 11 GAMES, FINED $25,000.
newsitem.headline: NBA-RODMAN SUSPENDED AT LEAST 11 GAMES, FINED $25,000.

text.p: Chicago Bulls forward Dennis Rodman was suspended at least through next month's All-Star Game and fined $25,000 by the NBA on Friday for kicking a courtside cameraman in Wednesday night's game at Minnesota.

The length of the suspension is pending discussions with a counsellor designated by the NBA. The Bulls play 11 more games before the All-Star break on February 9, including Friday night's home contest against Milwaukee.

"Until Dennis can provide meaningful assurances that he will conform his conduct on the playing court to acceptable standards -- including not placing others at physical risk -- his suspension will continue," said NBA Commissioner David Stern in a statement issued Friday.
The lost playing time could cost Rodman about $1 million in non-deferred salary and possible incentives, said Bulls vice president Jerry Krause.

Rodman kicked a courtside cameraman, Eugene Amos, after falling out of bounds in the third quarter of Wednesday's 112-102 win at Minnesota. Amos was carried off the court on a stretcher and claimed he was kicked in the groin.

"(For) any young kid who plays the game of basketball, I really feel it's important for them to know that Dennis may be a great player, but this particular type of behaviour towards other people, kicking other people, is wrong," Amos said Friday.
Rodman had said he kicked the cameraman in the knee.
"I just kicked him in the knee," said Rodman after the game. "He got carried off on a stretcher. It looked a little bit dramatic to me."

The suspension will likely end up as the second longest in NBA history, second only to the 26-game ban given to Kermit Washington of the Los Angeles Lakers for punching Rudy Tomjanovich of Houston in 1972.
Rodman was unavailable for comment Friday but Krause said he discussed the issue with Rodman Friday morning.
"He told me how bad he feels about the situation," Krause said. "I've been with Dennis before in these types of situations and he's always very remorseful afterwards."

Rodman stumbled out of bounds after fighting for a rebound. As he fell over a photographer, Amos turned his camera on Rodman. While sitting on the floor, Rodman kicked Amos high in his left thigh. Amos slumped over for more than five minutes before he was carried off.
Rodman, who finished with 15 rebounds, was not assessed a technical nor was he ejected, but Stern stressed the seriousness of the incident.
"We are not going to tolerate uncivilized behaviour," Stern said.

It is the second suspension of the season for Rodman, who served a two-game team-imposed suspension earlier this season for a profanity-laced tirade on the referees after a December 8 loss at Toronto. That suspension cost him $219,512, or 2/82nd of his 1996-97 salary of $9 million.

The five-time rebounding champion with the multi-coloured hair and multiple tattoos has had numerous run-ins with officials, including the head-butting of a referee last March at New Jersey that earned him a six-game suspension.
Upon his return, he kept his emotions in check and helped Chicago post a record 72-10 mark and its fourth championship in six years.

Since joining the Bulls from San Antonio in 1995, Rodman has cultivated a "lovable bad boy" image that placed him ninth among sports figures in 1996 earnings with $12.9 million, according to Forbes Magazine.
The 35-year-old Rodman began his career with the Detroit in 1986 and helped the Pistons win consecutive titles in 1989 and 1990. He was named NBA Defensive Player of the Year in 1990 and 1991.
